corrections.issue: Wrong speaker: the Nvidia 100-to-200 example is Kaminski circling back to her own opening Nvidia remark after saying she has been fascinated with trend following 'my entire career'; the host made the classical-trend-following-survives-AI point.
corrections.fix: Kaminski: even if an AI had predicted Nvidia's rise two years ago, a simple trend model would have captured it because a price moving from 100 to 200 must pass through 105 and 110, which is all the information trend followers need.

corrections.issue: Two speakers are blended: Kaminski's statement is that trend following does not predict and follows whatever themes move, asking why later; the large-language-model point (LLMs aim at prediction, so prediction is a 'red card' to AI in trend following) is the host's.
corrections.fix: Kaminski: trend following does not get hung up on predicting and follows the themes (Nvidia or cocoa), asking why later; the host adds that LLMs are built to predict, so a strategy built on not predicting gains nothing from them.

corrections.issue: The over- and under-reaction mechanism was stated by Kaminski, not the host; the host's point was that classical trend following using old price-history techniques will keep working despite AI, as it did after the internet.
corrections.fix: Kaastrup-Larsen expects classical trend following to do well despite AI because it is based on human behaviour and survived the internet-era claim that equal data kills it; the over/under-reaction mechanism was added by Kaminski.

completeness_estimate: 0.70 - first reader caught the main ETF structure, use-cases, replication trade-offs and AI view; it missed several secondary points (route taxonomy, hybrid, fee incentives, AUM caveats) and three speaker attributions in the AI section.
